title.value: Evaluating Dependencies in Fact Editing for Language Models: Specificity and Implication Awareness
title.justification: The paper focuses on the evaluation of dependencies in fact editing within language models, highlighting specificity and implication awareness as key components.
title.quote: Evaluating Dependencies in Fact Editing for Language Models: Specificity and Implication Awareness

extractions.description: This paper discusses the use of large language models (LLMs) as knowledge bases and addresses the issues in editing learned facts. It proposes a new evaluation protocol, DepEdit, to manage the knowledge in LLMs, ensuring edits respect internal logical constraints such as specificity and implication awareness. The paper presents experiments showing that existing methods struggle to infer implications of edited facts, proposing future work to better integrate dependency resolution in LLMs.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the internal mechanics of language models and knowledge editing, rather than addressing climate or ecological sustainability issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: While the potential of LLMs as KBs is recognized, their reliability remains contentious. The data used to train LLMs may contain inaccuracies or outdated information, compromising the trustworthiness of using LLMs as KBs.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any climate or ecological sustainable development themes, but rather on improving language model functionalities.
primary_category.quote: Our work adopts a broader perspective on knowledge editing and focuses on its capability to incorporate dependencies that encapsulates both specificity and implication awareness.

secondary_categories.justification: The content is centered around language models and does not extend to secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainability.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose to evaluate the specificity and implication awareness of knowledge editing methods in LLMs.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories provided are specific to climate and ecological issues, and this paper is unrelated to those.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our experiments reveal limitations in current knowledge editing techniques, both in terms of specificity and their ability to understand implications.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The secondary sub-categories are not relevant as the paper does not address issues of climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: To implement our evaluation protocol, we collect a new question-answering dataset DepEdit with If-then rules in natural language.

applications.justification: The paper's applications are aimed at improving the functionality of LLMs rather than addressing climate or ecological challenges.
applications.quote: We propose a new evaluation protocol called establish-and-update and an accompanying English question-answering dataset (DepEdit) for a comprehensive evaluation of dependency in editing LLMs.

new_primary_category.justification: No new categories are suggested as the paper does not address climate or ecological sustainable development issues.
new_primary_category.quote: Our evaluation protocol is inspired by the principles of knowledge editing in knowledge bases.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-categories are introduced since the paper is not aligned with climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Each simulation focuses on a subset of the dataset, where we are able to control the entities, relations and applicable If-Then rules described within this subset.
